title: Localization of shifted derived Hom from a bounded-below compact source
statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $R_t=R[1/t]$, the sheafified section localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], and $F:D(R)\to D(R_t)$ for the functor induced termwise by exact scalar localization $M\mapsto R_t\otimes_R M$, with sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the exact-functor derived construction [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Fix $K\in D(R)$ with the following property: for every countable family $(L_n)$ with a common cohomological lower bound and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L_n[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,(\bigoplus_nL_n)[q])$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded-below $L\in D(R)$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the actual scalar-extension map induces an isomorphism of $A[1/t]$-modules
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L[q])[1/t]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_t)}(FK,FL[q]),\qquad u/t^n\longmapsto t^{-n}F(u).$$
Localization of the Hom module has the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. These isomorphisms are natural in $K,L$, commute with shifts, and respect identity maps and composition whenever the displayed hypotheses hold for the objects involved. No constructibility, scheme, or essential-surjectivity assertion is included.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and proof of Proposition 6.8.14(2); abstract ringed-site telescope argument extracted from the item, with coproduct continuity as an explicit hypothesis

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-sheaf-exact] with $s$ the image of $t$. For $U=\operatorname{Res}_{R\to R_t}$, [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] gives exact restriction and the ordinary adjunction with unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The construction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] localizes this exact adjunction termwise, yielding $F\dashv U$ with the same unit $\eta$ in the derived category. Its unit commutes with shifts because the termwise maps do.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), exact adjunction localized termwise; ordinary adjunction as in sites-modules.tex

proof.text: For bounded-below $L$, [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-underlying-telescope] makes $UFL[q]$ the telescope of $L[q]\xrightarrow{t}L[q]\to\cdots$, with stage-$n$ leg $U(t^{-n})\eta_{L[q]}$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sequence-relative-hom-telescope] to this triangle. Its two coproduct hypotheses are precisely the assumption on $K$ for the constant families $L[q]$ and $L[q+1]$, each with a common lower bound. Thus $\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}(K,L[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,UFL[q])$, with transition $u\mapsto tu$ and stage map $u\mapsto U(t^{-n})\eta_{L[q]}u$.

source.place: Tags 093W, 0CRK and 094A; sequence-relative Hom telescope calculation

proof.text: Compose with the adjunction from Step 1. Naturality of its unit gives $\eta_{L[q]}u=UF(u)\eta_K$; the triangle identity says the adjunct of $U(g)\eta_K$ is $g$. Taking $g=t^{-n}F(u)$ shows that the stage-$n$ map is exactly $u\mapsto t^{-n}F(u)$.

source.place: Tag 015F; naturality of the localized unit and the adjunction triangle identity

proof.text: Write $H=\operatorname{Hom}(K,L[q])$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], $H[1/t]$ is the preceding colimit: $u/t^n=v/t^m$ iff $t^k(t^mu-t^nv)=0$ for some $k$, precisely equality at a common later stage. Hence the bijection is $u/t^n\mapsto t^{-n}F(u)$. For the canonical actions [def-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-coefficient-actions], scalar extension sends $au$ to $aF(u)$ already termwise; localization preserves this equation. On fractions, $(a/t^r)(u/t^n)=au/t^{r+n}$, proving $A[1/t]$-linearity.

source.place: Tags 07JZ and 07K0, module fraction relation and universal property

proof.text: Precomposition by $h$ and postcomposition by $v$ give respectively $t^{-n}F(u)F(h)$ and $F(v)t^{-n}F(u)$, proving naturality. Shifting the formula gives $t^{-n}F(u)[r]$ under the termwise shift comparisons. The identity fraction maps to $F(1)=1$, and the composite of $u/t^n$ and $v/t^m$ maps to $t^{-(m+n)}F(vu)=(t^{-m}F(v))(t^{-n}F(u))$. Every element is a fraction, so these equations give all asserted compatibilities whenever the comparisons exist.
